sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196], but the path was a step change followed by a plateau: growth ran 104.0% in FY2017 and 64.2% in FY2021 [D36][D218], then collapsed to 0.1% in FY2023 [D311] before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D358][D406].

The FY2017 loss of $3,445.1 million [F32] was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation expense primarily related to the CEO award and RSUs whose performance condition was satisfied at the IPO [P74].

The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening 98.7% to $1,395.3 million [F17][D264], came as Adjusted EBITDA fell on increased cost of revenue and overall operating expenses, partially offset by increased revenues [P42].

Since then the operating loss has narrowed every year, from $1,398.4 million in FY2023 to $532.2 million in FY2025 [F18][F20], and the operating margin of -9.0% is the best in the window against a median of -32.4% [F30][D555].

North America remains the largest pool at 58.6% of revenue in FY2025 [D456], but it contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D458][D406], while Rest of world at 23.0% of revenue [D497] added 3.7pp [D499] and Europe at 18.4% [D522] added 2.5pp [D524].

Advertising revenue rose 5.8% to $5,186.1 million, contributing 5.3pp [S39][D537][D538], as global advertising impressions volume grew about 17% on expanded delivery within Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression [P24].
Other revenue grew 62.9% to $745.4 million and contributed 5.4pp [S42][D544][D545], predominantly on higher subscription revenue from subscriber growth [P24].
Profit grew faster than revenue: operating costs rose 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth [D423][D406], an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D429].
Per-share losses fell 35.7% to -$0.27 [F60][D409], slightly less than the 34.0% fall in net loss [D408], because diluted shares rose 2.1% to 1,694.6 million [X150][D425].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% [F30] is 5.7pp better than FY2024 [D419] and far above the window median of -32.4% and low of -422.5% [D555][D553].

Cost of revenue fell to 45.0% of revenue from 46.1%, adding 1.1pp to margin [D386][D338][D431], and R&D fell to 30.2% from 31.6%, adding 1.3pp [D387][D339][D432], with the residual other lines adding 3.3pp [D433].

The R&D line rose 6.0% in dollars [D422] on investments in product development and higher employee compensation from additional headcount, partly offset by $38.8 million of restructuring charges recognized in 2024 [P23].

Selling and marketing fell 4.0% in dollars [X49][X50] on the timing of marketing events in the prior year, lower advertising and marketing investments, and $19.9 million of 2024 restructuring charges [P22].

Net margin of -7.8% [F50] sits 1.2pp above operating margin [F30] because other income of $68.9 million [X130] included $96.7 million of gains on note extinguishment [P18], partly offset by interest expense of $122.0 million [X100] that rose $100.4 million on the new 2033 and 2034 Notes [P19].

Operating cash flow of $656.2 million exceeded the $460.5 million net loss [F80][F40], and free cash flow of $437.2 million was a 7.4% margin, the window high against a median of -4.1% [F100][D393][D560][D561].

Operating cash flow rose from $413.5 million [F79] primarily on non-cash items, including stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Capital intensity is low: capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue [F90][D392] and 1.34x D&A of $163.6 million [D395][X80], with purchases primarily for improvements to leased facilities [P10].

Cash generation now rests heavily on adding back $1,016.8 million of stock-based compensation [X90], which is 155.0% of operating cash flow [D396], so the quality of the conversion depends on a cost that is real to shareholders.

The company moved from $1,439.8 million of net cash in FY2021 [D211] to $596.3 million of net debt in FY2025 [D399], as cash and investments fell 12.9% to $2,940.6 million [D397][D426] while total debt of $3,536.8 million was only 2.9% lower [D398][D427].

Net cash is -10.1% of revenue [D400], in the 0th percentile against internet peers whose median is 45.0% [D578][D579], and the current ratio of 3.56x is the window low against a median of 5.15x [F180][D565][D567].
In February 2025 the company repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026, 2027 and 2028 Notes for cash [P1], funded by $1.47 billion of net proceeds from new 2033 Notes [P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million [X156] were 171.7% of free cash flow [D402], and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D425], so repurchases have not offset issuance.
With $3.4 billion of non-cancelable commitments due mostly within two years [P14], the thin net cash position leaves less room than the peer median implies.
The company has reported a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40]; the loss is narrowing but has never closed.
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390][D22], which is 191.1% of the operating loss [D404].

Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D211][D256][D304][D351][D399], and buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402].
The buyback overfunding is the most concerning of these because it converts a cash-generative year into a further draw on a balance sheet that already sits below every peer on net cash.
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 level of -9.0% [F30] or slips back toward the -32.4% median [D555], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the FY2025 high of 7.4% [D560] or falls back toward the -4.1% median [D561], with stock-based compensation at 17.1% of revenue [D390] the swing factor.
Whether net cash returns above zero from the FY2025 level of -$596.3 million [D399], given buybacks at 171.7% of free cash flow [D402] and $3.4 billion of commitments [P14].
Whether Other revenue keeps contributing more than 5.4pp of growth [D545] as its share rises from 12.6% [D543], or advertising growth of 5.8% [D537] has to carry the total alone.
